answer: In this PoA design, every identity posts bonded collateral. Correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities incurs a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), rather than k separate fines. Upon detection, the swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss, with asymmetric depreciation eroding residual collateral; thus controlling many identities is economically irrational: an ocean of accounts becomes a hollow liability when linked signatures reveal the prism of coordination.
